assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for correlated insulators, unconventional superconductivity and magnetism. It is a rare case where an electronic-structure prediction (continuum band-structure theory) preceded and then guided a field-defining experiment. Originality and lasting impact are very high, and the physics sits at the core of what first-principles and model electronic-structure theory aims to explain.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical prediction of the magic angle is credited to MacDonald and Bistritzer; the decisive 2018 observation of correlated and superconducting states is Jarillo-Herrero's group. Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands and van Hove singularities is independent and important. A three-person prize needs a theory-plus-experiment choice; I would favour MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, with the third slot between Andrei and Bistritzer unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated states and superconductivity, and the field is broad and stable. The mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself is mature enough for recognition, roughly eight years after the key experiments.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Fair division of credit between Bistritzer, MacDonald, Andrei and Jarillo-Herrero is contested and I cannot independently verify the details of priority.
Sample-to-sample variation in twist-angle disorder complicates reproducibility claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators changed how band structure is classified, linking spin-orbit coupling, symmetry and topology to protected surface and edge states. The concept is original, widely confirmed and has spread through materials theory and computation, including large first-principles searches for topological materials. Lasting impact is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall proposal; Molenkamp's group gave the first HgTe quantum spin Hall experiment following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction; Hasan's ARPES work established three-dimensional topological insulators. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and others are not on the supplied credit list, so any prize drawn only from these names is an incomplete picture of the field. Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan seems the most defensible subset among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is extensive and independent, over nearly two decades. The interpretation is stable. Timing is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors outside the credited list (for example the HgTe theory proposal) complicate fair allocation.
Whether Mele or Hasan has the stronger claim to the third slot is not settled by the supplied record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and then giant TMR in crystalline MgO barriers made spin-dependent tunnelling a technology (read heads, MRAM) and a testing ground for spin-polarized transport theory. The MgO coherent-tunnelling mechanism was predicted by first-principles calculations, which gives the discovery a clean theory-experiment link. Impact is large and clearly physical, though it follows GMR, already recognized in 2007.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995. Yuasa and Parkin independently reported large MgO TMR in 2004. Theoretical predictions (Butler, Mathon) are not in the credit list. With at most three names, one must leave out either Miyazaki or one of the MgO pair; I would give priority to Moodera, Yuasa and Parkin but this is a hard cut.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and commercialized for fifteen to thirty years. Recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Four credited names for three slots and parallel independent discoveries make credit allocation difficult.
Applied/technological weight may be judged to outweigh fundamental novelty relative to GMR.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combined the magic-wavelength lattice idea with narrow optical transitions to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 or below, a transformative advance in precision measurement with applications to fundamental-constant tests, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The idea is clear, original and demonstrably realized.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice concept; Ye drove the experimental realization to the highest accuracy and stability. A two-person configuration is straightforward and natural. Other optical-clock work (ion clocks, combs) was already recognized in 2005 and 2012.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare lattice clocks, performance has improved steadily, and the interpretation is stable. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with Jun Ye's other credited work (ultracold molecules) is not an issue for attribution but may influence relative committee appetite.
Whether the committee views this as incremental to earlier precision-spectroscopy prizes is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a non-perturbative, controlled framework for strongly correlated electrons, capturing the Mott transition and Hubbard bands, and forming the basis of DFT+DMFT for real materials. As someone who works with electronic-structure methods, I regard its importance for realistic treatment of correlated solids as very high, although its status as a discovery of nature as opposed to a method is a legitimate concern.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt's infinite-dimension limit and Georges and Kotliar's mapping to the Anderson impurity model are decisive, together with Müller-Hartmann and Georges-Kotliar-Krauth-Rozenberg's review work. Metzner is not on the supplied list, so a prize built from these names omits a key originator. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are the natural trio among those supplied.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for more than three decades, with experimental comparisons via spectroscopy and cold-atom realizations. Maturity is high, but quantitative accuracy for specific materials is mixed.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner (and others) from the credited names.
Method-versus-discovery question: a Nobel committee may prefer physical discoveries over computational frameworks.
DMFT neglects non-local correlations, so reach for low-dimensional systems is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realized Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, including the superfluid-Mott transition, fermionic Mott insulators and antiferromagnetic correlations. It gives direct access to many-body physics that connects to the correlated-electron problems I study, and it has matured into a major field.
assessment.attribution: Theoretical proposal (Jaksch, Zoller) overlaps with the credited Cirac and Zoller; the decisive experiments are Greiner and Bloch (Mott transition, 2002) and Esslinger (fermionic Hubbard and Mott insulator). Five credited names exceed the three-laureate limit and Greiner-Bloch versus Esslinger versus theory is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many labs; quantum-gas microscopes now resolve single sites. Timing is reasonable, though Bose-Einstein condensation was recognized in 2001 and the 2012 prize touched quantum control of atoms.
uncertainties: Five credited names and an unresolved theory-versus-experiment split.
Potential perception that this overlaps with prior cold-atom prizes.
Open question whether quantum simulation has yet produced decisive new physics on contested problems like d-wave superconductivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order, with compensated moments yet spin-split bands set by crystal symmetry. This is directly within my field of magnetism and the electronic-structure description is elegant and testable. It could matter for spintronics through spin-split currents without net magnetization.
assessment.attribution: The 2022 classification papers and earlier prediction work by Šmejkal, Jungwirth, Sinova and collaborators credit these three well, though earlier symmetry-based work by Hayami, Yuan and others, and Mazin's contributions, complicate priority. The supplied three are a plausible core but I cannot verify the priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation (ARPES in MnTe and CrSb, magnetic circular dichroism and related) arrived in 2024-2025 and is promising but young. Recognition now would likely be premature; I rank it high for potential rather than readiness.
uncertainties: Short track record, only a few years of independent confirmation.
Priority disputes with earlier symmetry-based predictions and with Mazin and others.
Technological relevance remains largely prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin ice and the emergent magnetic monopole picture are an elegant example of emergent quasiparticles and fractionalization in a frustrated magnet, with a clear connection to Coulomb-phase and Dirac-string ideas. It is important magnetism physics, with conceptual reach beyond one material.
assessment.attribution: Moessner and Sondhi are credited for theory of frustrated-magnet physics; Bramwell for experimental work on spin-ice materials. The monopole proposal is by Castelnovo, Moessner and Sondhi, and the experimental discovery of spin ice by Harris, Bramwell and others; some of these are not in the credited names, so allocation is incomplete and uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic evidence (Morris, Fennell and others in 2009) support the monopole picture, but quantitative details such as monopole dynamics have been debated, and the field has not produced a single clean decisive experiment.
uncertainties: Key originators (such as Castelnovo and early spin-ice experimentalists) are not in the credited list.
The experimental evidence for true monopole dynamics is somewhat contested.
Impact beyond fundamental interest is limited.
